step1_analysis.description: A series RLC resonant circuit representing the passive tank of a Q-enhanced LC filter. The active cross-coupled pair for Q-enhancement (which provides negative resistance) is not present in this extracted netlist, leaving only the passive components and their parasitic resistances.

paper_reference.title: A 2.5-GHz Low-Power, High Dynamic Range, Self-Tuned Q-Enhanced LC Filter in SOI

resonant_frequency.description: The center frequency where the LC tank resonates.

sky130_expected.calculation: f0 = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(L_tot * C1)). With L1=L2=1nH and C1=2pF, f0 = 2.51 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by the passive L and C values chosen to match the paper's target frequency.

quality_factor.description: The Q-factor of the passive tank, determining the sharpness of the resonance.

sky130_expected.calculation: Q = (1 / R_tot) * sqrt(L_tot / C1). With R_tot = 4 ohms, L_tot = 2nH, C1 = 2pF, Q = 7.9.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Without the active Q-enhancement circuit, the Q-factor is limited by the parasitic series resistances of the inductors and the source resistance.

peak_gain.description: The voltage gain at the resonant frequency.

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain = 20 * log10(Q). For Q=7.9, Gain = 17.9 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The passive voltage gain across the capacitor in a series RLC circuit is proportional to the Q-factor.

sky130_expected.calculation: BW = f0 / Q. For f0=2.5GHz and Q=7.9, BW = 316 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The passive bandwidth is much wider than the paper's reported 70 MHz because the active Q-enhancement is missing.

step3_testbench.description: AC analysis to measure the resonant frequency and peak gain of the passive LC tank.
